title: INMOTION study on contactless monitoring of vital signs in a sleep laboratory
summary:
Sleep studies in children are currently conducted using many cables and sensors attached directly to the body. This is often uncomfortable and stressful for children, and the examination can only be carried out in specially equipped sleep laboratories.

This study investigates whether modern, contactless measuring devices – such as radar, camera and microphone sensors – can reliably record important body functions like breathing, heart rate and movement during sleep, without the need to attach any sensors directly to the body. The study also examines whether artificial intelligence can make the analysis of this data faster and more accurate.

The contactless measuring devices are placed in the room of the sleep laboratory and record additional data during the sleep study that the child is already scheduled to undergo. This data is not used for medical treatment, but solely for scientific analysis. The goal is to use this data to develop and train computer programs that can detect sleep patterns and body functions in the future without the need for body-worn sensors.

interventions.name:
Prospective, interventional study. 
In addition to the routine measurement for therapeutic purposes (PSG), a second, non-invasive measurement is carried out for scientific purposes. The clinical routine is not affected by the study, and the data collected are not incorporated into clinical treatmen

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Included are patients for whom a polygraph test or polysomnography has been ordered.
Exclusion criteria:
None
